name: Test Data Management Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any test data management task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any test data management task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any test data management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Validate test data management outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
3. Keep test data management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to test data management (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen test data management approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Document any non-obvious test data management decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
7. Keep test data management changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
8. When test data management decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
9. When test data management guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
10. Before starting test data management work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
11. When multiple test data management strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
12. State assumptions about test data management explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic test data management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop test data management edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of test data management correctness.
- Do not skip documenting test data management assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about test data management over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
